answer: Give each new agent zero weight until ninety days of steady, non-transferable history: finished jobs, settled payments, and peer attestations that cannot be sold or copied to another key. A sybil farm cannot buy calendar time, so a thousand fresh shells stay voiceless however fast they are spun up. Keeping them alive for ninety days at fifty cents a day in fees and upkeep costs about $45,000 before a single weighted vote — a delta anyone can verify, like judging a sonnet by all fourteen lines, not one borrowed verse, or a walnut by its kernel, not its shell.
